Exact, Jastrow and RBM overlap distributions¶

System sizes: periodic kagome, three spins per unit cell, $N=3L^2$. The original exact/variational sections use $L=2$, $2\times2$ unit cells, $N=12$ spins. The measured larger-system sections use $L=4$, $4\times4$ unit cells, $N=48$ spins. All results use $h=0.15$.

Where are the $L=4$ results? Scroll to L=4, N=48: before and after projection, followed by L=4, N=48: higher-field distributions. The $L=2$ exact-guide, exact-ground-state, guide-MCMC and GFMC comparison appears immediately before them. Plot-panel counts are not lattice sizes.

This follows exact_guide_overlap_distributions.ipynb: two independent spin configurations of the same disorder give $q=N^{-1}\sum_i s_i t_i$. For $L=2$, $N=12$, there are 13 allowed values from -1 to 1, spaced by 1/6. The plotted ordinate is probability mass per bin, whose heights sum to one. Connecting lines are visual aids, not a continuous density.

$$P_J(q)=\sum_{s,t}p_J(s)p_J(t)\,\mathbf1[N^{-1}s\cdot t=q].$$

Exact uses $p=\psi_0^2$; each unprojected guide uses normalized $p=\psi_T^2$. The XOR/Walsh convolution matches the original notebook. Normalization and first/second moments are independently checked from magnetizations and pairs. The original exact/variational plots in this first part are unprojected. Saved GFMC moment spectra cannot reconstruct the full $P(q)$; a separate histogram estimator would be required.

The first comparison shows the four existing diagnostic contexts at $h=0.15$. Guides were fitted using full-basis variational energy, without ground-state labels. Minimum-energy seed selection precedes evaluation. This is an L2 ansatz/optimization test, not scalable sampled-training validation.

L=2, N=12: All optimization seeds¶

Faint curves retain every seed, including fits trapped in another sector. A good selected curve does not imply reliable optimization. These panels show individual disorders, so no disorder error bars are attached. TV is half the sum of absolute bin-probability differences from exact and lies between zero and one.

L=2, N=12: Guides learned with sampled VMC¶

These fits used parallel-tempering samples during training. Each panel shows both seeds and direct/continuation schedules; no seed is selected. The curves are computed from frozen guide probabilities after training, using L2-only enumeration to remove histogram sampling noise. In this original campaign, continuation used more updates than direct training. A separate matched-update field campaign addresses that confound.

L=2, N=12: Gradually increasing Gamma: physical structure and numerical reliability¶

Hold $h=0.15$ and each disorder fixed. Fields are 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.85 and 1.00. The eight IDs 50000–50007 form the matched disorder set; 50043 is shown separately as a difficult-case diagnostic. Compute $P_J$ first, then average across disorders; never pair states from different disorders. Error bars are one descriptive standard error across disorders, not training uncertainty or Monte Carlo error.

We track exact overlap variance and gap separately from guide TV, spectral error and seed reliability. Broad or changing P(q) in L2 is evidence of a finite-size crossover, not a thermodynamic phase. Convergence failure cannot define a phase. A candidate field needs both retained physical structure and stable algorithms; this full-basis fit screen alone cannot qualify GFMC or larger L.

L=2, N=12: Candidate field region¶

The completed full-basis screen identifies $\Gamma=0.60$–$0.70$ as an RBM candidate window. On disorder 50043 the exact negative-overlap shoulder grows through this interval while the selected RBM TV error falls from 0.0060 to 0.0016. At $\Gamma=0.65$, TV is 0.0022 and connected-spectrum error is 0.94%. All three RBM seeds on this disorder have TV below 0.01 from 0.60 onward. Across the separate eight-disorder ensemble, all 24 RBM seeds have TV below 0.05 from 0.60 onward. These descriptive thresholds do not certify ground-state sampling.

Jastrow remains unreliable here: its selected TV on 50043 rises to 0.243 at 0.65. The apparent window is therefore ansatz-dependent. Negative-overlap weight alone is not a phase identifier; it can also rise as a distribution approaches a symmetric paramagnet. The shoulder and two maxima in this small system are features to follow with size, not evidence of thermodynamic replica symmetry breaking.

Two independent follow-ups have been launched on AutoDL: equal-update sampled VMC at $L=2,4$ (1200 updates per fit, direct versus continuation), and CT GFMC population/time sensitivity over all eight fields. Their live records are under data/kagome/ltfim_simple_overlap_v1/sampled/ and projector/. This notebook's field recommendation is based on the completed full-basis screen; it does not claim those follow-ups have converged.

Saved disorder averages: sizes, Hamiltonian and provenance¶

The following results are frozen measurements from the completed companion reports. Snapshot dates and ensemble coverage are printed by the loading cells. They are not a live campaign status.

Sizes: L=2, N=12 and L=4, N=48; periodic boundaries; h=0.15.

Shared protocol¶

Periodic kagome nearest-neighbor bonds are generated once per disorder sample, with $$H=\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}K_{ij}Z_iZ_j-h\sum_i Z_i-\Gamma\sum_i X_i, \qquad K_{ij}=1+0.5u_{ij},\quad u_{ij}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim U(-1,1).$$ Thus $K_{ij}\sim U(0.5,1.5)$, independently on each undirected nearest-neighbor edge; all bonds are antiferromagnetic and their mean strength sets the energy unit. Frustration comes from kagome geometry. The implementation stores $J_{ij}=-K_{ij}$ in the equivalent convention $-\sum J_{ij}Z_iZ_j$. For reproducibility, NumPy default_rng(SeedSequence([20261027, L, sample_id, 1])) draws one uniform variate per bond in the lattice bond-list order; the final 1 specifies periodic boundaries. These are quenched couplings: the same bonds are held fixed through training, MC and projection, across both guide families, all seeds and every $\Gamma$ for a given $(L,\mathrm{sample\_id})$. $L=2$ uses IDs 50000–50007 and $L=4$ uses 60000–60007. Different sizes have different bond realizations, even if an ID is reused. Couplings are never selected or reweighted by the observed shape of $P(q)$.

Only disorder averages are shown at $\Gamma=0.60,0.65$. The $L=2$ panels overlay exact guide, exact ground-state, and available MC/GFMC curves; $L=4$ uses before projection and after projection columns. Each curve gives equal weight to eight disorders. Capped error bars are $\pm1$ standard error of the disorder mean ($s_J/\sqrt{8}$), pointwise in $q$. They describe finite-ensemble variation and do not bound mixing, finite-population or finite-forward-time errors.

$q=N^{-1}\sum_i s_i t_i$ uses independent physical replicas of the same disorder. $P(q)$ is probability mass per allowed overlap; connecting lines are visual aids. The next two figures show $L=2$ with exact and Monte Carlo comparisons, then $L=4$. All outputs were computed and executed on AutoDL.

load=lambda name: json.loads((folder/name).read_text())

l2=load('guide_distributions_l2.json')['rows']

if not allow_pending:

assert all(r['replay_verified'] for r in projected if r['task']['L']==4)

def mean_se(values):
    a=np.asarray(values,dtype=float)
    assert len(a)==8
    np.testing.assert_allclose(a.sum(1),1,atol=1e-12)
    return a.mean(0),a.std(0,ddof=1)/np.sqrt(len(a))
def curve(ax,q,values,label,color,fmt='o-',alpha=1):
    if q is None:
        ax.text(.03,.96-.065*len(ax.texts),label+' pending (complete ensemble required)',
                transform=ax.transAxes,va='top',fontsize=7,color=color)
        return
    mean,se=mean_se(values)
    ax.errorbar(q,mean,yerr=se,fmt=fmt,color=color,ms=3,lw=1.15,
                elinewidth=.75,capsize=2,capthick=.75,label=label,alpha=alpha)
def guide_group(rows,L,g,kind):
    group=[r for r in rows if r['task']['L']==L and r['task']['gamma']==g
           and r['task']['kind']==kind and r.get('selected',True)]
    group=sorted(group,key=lambda r:r['task']['sample_id'])
    if allow_pending and len(group)!=8:
        return None,None
    assert len(group)==8 and len({r['task']['sample_id'] for r in group})==8
    return np.array(group[0]['q_grid']),np.array([np.mean([s['mass'] for s in r['starts']],axis=0) for r in group])
def projected_group(L,g,kind):
    group=[r for r in projected if (r['task']['L'],r['task']['gamma'],r['task']['kind'])==(L,g,kind)]
    ids=sorted({r['task']['sample_id'] for r in group})
    if allow_pending and (len(group)!=16 or len(ids)!=8):
        return None,None
    assert len(group)==16 and len(ids)==8
    values=[]
    for sid in ids:
        rs=[r for r in group if r['task']['sample_id']==sid]
        assert {r['task']['repeat'] for r in rs}=={0,1}
        values.append(np.mean([r['mass'] for r in rs],axis=0))
    return np.array(group[0]['q_grid']),np.array(values)
def finish(fig,name):
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(figures/(name+'.png'),dpi=180,bbox_inches='tight')
    fig.savefig(figures/(name+'.pdf'),bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()
def axes_style(axes):
    for ax in axes.flat:
        ax.set(xlabel='q',ylabel='Disorder mean P(q) mass',xlim=(-1.03,1.03))
        ax.grid(alpha=.2); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
print('Frozen L=4 production snapshot:',load('snapshot.json')['created_utc'])
print('Chosen longitudinal field: h=0.15 (fixed); transverse fields: Gamma=0.60, 0.65.')
print(f'Completed histogram measurements: {len(projected)}/128 GFMC runs and {len(l2)}/32 L=2 guide MC tasks; eight disorders per plotted curve.')
for L in [2,4]:
    for g in [.6,.65]:
        for kind in ['jastrow','rbm_2']:
            before=guide_group(l2 if L==2 else guides,L,g,kind)[0] is not None
            after=projected_group(L,g,kind)[0] is not None
            print(f'L={L}, Gamma={g:.2f}, {names[kind]}: before MC {"complete" if before else "pending"}; after GFMC {"complete" if after else "pending"}')

L=2, N=12: exact guides, ground state, MCMC and GFMC¶

$L=2$: all comparisons on the same axes. Each panel overlays exact enumeration of the trained Jastrow and RBM guide distributions (colored dashed curves with triangle markers), the exact ground-state distribution (black squares), and available guide MCMC (colored dots without connecting lines) and pure GFMC estimates (colored solid curves with circles). One panel is shown per $\Gamma$. All curves use disorder IDs 50000–50007. The two guide families use their previously selected energy-trained fits. MC starts and repeats are averaged within each disorder before computing the disorder mean and its error bars.

L=4, N=48: before and after projection¶

4 × 4 unit cells, three spins per cell, periodic boundaries in both directions. There are 49 allowed overlaps with spacing 1/24.

$L=4$: before and after projection. Both columns use disorder IDs 60000–60007 and the same selected frozen guides. Before projection uses MCMC with random/up/down starts. After projection uses four independently branching populations with descendant-weighted tagged configurations, 512 walkers per population, equilibration and forward times 16, eight cycles and two repeats. The histograms replay the frozen production trajectories; their first and second moments and connected spectra match those original records to $10^{-12}$. The $L=2$ and $L=4$ disorder ensembles are different.

L=4, N=48: higher-field distributions¶

These are measured pure GFMC overlap histograms for periodic kagome $L=4$ ($N=48$). Only complete ensembles with eight disorders and two repeats per disorder are shown. The same disorder IDs 60000–60007 have equal weight at every field and for both guides; no disorder is selected by its observed broadness. The exact $L=2$ and guide-MCMC comparisons are included earlier in this notebook.

The Hamiltonian is $$H=\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}K_{ij}Z_iZ_j-0.15\sum_iZ_i-\Gamma\sum_iX_i,$$ with iid antiferromagnetic bonds $K_{ij}\sim U(0.5,1.5)$, stored as $J_{ij}=-K_{ij}$. NumPy default_rng(SeedSequence([20261027,L,sample_id,1])) draws bonds in the periodic lattice bond-list order. Quenched bonds are reused across all fields, guides, and seeds for each size and disorder ID.

Each run uses four independently branching populations with 512 walkers each, equilibration and forward times 16, and eight cycles. Descendant-weighted configurations are pooled equally across cycles; all six cross-population pairs give $q=N^{-1}\sum_i s_i t_i$. Repeats are averaged within each disorder first. The higher-field histograms are deterministic replays of frozen production trajectories. Their $q,q^2$, and connected spectra must match production to $10^{-12}$. The $\Gamma=0.60,0.65$ histograms reuse the earlier verified measurements.

$P(q)$ denotes probability mass at each allowed overlap; connecting lines are visual aids. Capped bars give $\pm s_J/\sqrt8$ pointwise in $q$. Width bars use a delete-one-disorder jackknife. These errors exclude mixing and projection bias. All ancestry alarms retain equal disorder weight. The projections remain preliminary pending population, forward-time and starting-state sensitivity. Broadening alone does not establish glassiness, a transition, or finite-size drift. Computation, checks, plotting and notebook execution take place on AutoDL.

def width(a):
    mean=a.mean(0)
    return np.sqrt(max(0,float(q*q@mean-(q@mean)**2)))
def jackknife(a,stat):
    x=np.array([stat(np.delete(a,i,axis=0)) for i in range(8)])
    return float(np.sqrt(7/8*np.sum((x-x.mean())**2)))

L=4, N=48: uniform polarization and nonuniform overlap¶

For two independent replicas of the same disorder, let $m_{i,J}=\langle Z_i\rangle_J$ and $\bar m_J=N^{-1}\sum_i m_{i,J}$. Then $$\langle q\rangle_J=\frac1N\sum_i m_{i,J}^2 =\bar m_J^2+\frac1N\sum_i(m_{i,J}-\bar m_J)^2.$$ The first term measures the contribution of uniform polarization to the mean overlap. The second measures a reproducible nonuniform local pattern. We evaluate both terms within each disorder, then average the eight disorders equally: $[\bar m_J^2]_J$ is not $[\bar m_J]_J^2$. This decomposes the mean overlap, not the histogram width or peak height.

The hypothesis is that the sharp, high-overlap low-$\Gamma$ peaks reflect stronger freezing. A dominant nonuniform contribution would support the local pattern part of that interpretation and show that uniform polarization explains only a small fraction of the overlap. The inequality $h<\Gamma$ alone does not exclude ferromagnetic order. Nonuniform polarization can also arise from a field-pinned response to quenched disorder or other spatial order; it is not by itself a glass order parameter in a field.

Estimator: reconstruct each of the four populations' local magnetizations from saved descendant weights, averaging cycles first as in the measured $P(q)$. Use all six cross-population products for both terms, without squaring a noisy pooled estimate. Thus $\widehat{\bar m_J^2}$ uses $\bar m_J^{(a)}\bar m_J^{(b)}$, and the nonuniform term uses $N^{-1}\sum_i(m_{i,J}^{(a)}-\bar m_J^{(a)})(m_{i,J}^{(b)}-\bar m_J^{(b)})$. Finite-sample estimates are not clipped to zero. This is distinct from the single-snapshot second moment $\langle(N^{-1}\sum_i Z_i)^2\rangle$.

Two repeats are averaged within each disorder before the disorder mean and capped $\pm1$ disorder-SE bars. The nonuniform fraction is the ratio of disorder means; its error uses a delete-one-disorder jackknife. Errors exclude sampling and projection bias. Every ancestry alarm is retained with equal weight.

polarization_module=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(polarization_module)
polarization_runs=[]
for r in rows:
    t=r['task']
    assert t['L']==4 and t['audit']=='main' and r['replay_verified']
    raw_path=folder/r['raw_file']
    assert hashlib.sha256(raw_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==r['raw_sha256']
    with np.load(raw_path) as raw:
        result=polarization_module.polarization_components(raw['tags'],raw['counts'])
    q=np.asarray(r['q_grid']);mass=np.asarray(r['mass'])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(result['mean_q'],q@mass,atol=1e-12,rtol=0)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(result['mean_q'],r['q'],atol=1e-12,rtol=0)
    polarization_runs.append(dict(task=t,raw_file=r['raw_file'],raw_sha256=r['raw_sha256'],
        provenance=r['provenance'],ancestry_alarm=r['ancestry_alarm'],**result))
polarization_disorders=[];polarization_summary=[]
component_keys=['mean_q','uniform_squared','nonuniform']
for gamma,kind in sorted({(r['task']['gamma'],r['task']['kind']) for r in polarization_runs}):
    group=[r for r in polarization_runs if (r['task']['gamma'],r['task']['kind'])==(gamma,kind)]
    assert len(group)==16
    values=[]
    for sid in range(60000,60008):
        repeats=[r for r in group if r['task']['sample_id']==sid]
        assert sorted(r['task']['repeat'] for r in repeats)==[0,1]
        value=np.mean([[r[key] for key in component_keys] for r in repeats],axis=0)
        values.append(value)
        polarization_disorders.append(dict(L=4,N=48,gamma=gamma,kind=kind,sample_id=sid,
            **dict(zip(component_keys,map(float,value))),
            ancestry_alarms=sum(r['ancestry_alarm'] for r in repeats)))
    values=np.asarray(values)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(values[:,0],values[:,1]+values[:,2],atol=1e-12,rtol=0)
    means=values.mean(axis=0);errors=values.std(axis=0,ddof=1)/np.sqrt(8)
    leave=np.asarray([np.delete(values,i,axis=0).mean(axis=0) for i in range(8)])
    assert means[0]>0 and (leave[:,0]>0).all(), 'Nonuniform fraction requires nonzero mean overlap'
    fractions=leave[:,2]/leave[:,0]
    fraction_se=float(np.sqrt(7/8*np.sum((fractions-fractions.mean())**2)))
    polarization_summary.append(dict(L=4,N=48,gamma=gamma,kind=kind,
        **dict(zip(component_keys,map(float,means))),
        **{key+'_se':float(error) for key,error in zip(component_keys,errors)},
        nonuniform_fraction=float(means[2]/means[0]),nonuniform_fraction_se=fraction_se,
        ancestry_alarms=sum(r['ancestry_alarm'] for r in group),disorders=8,runs=16))

    table.append([f"{r['gamma']:.2f}",names[r['kind']],
        *[f"{r[key]:.5f} ± {r[key+'_se']:.5f}" for key in component_keys],
        f"{r['nonuniform_fraction']:.3f} ± {r['nonuniform_fraction_se']:.3f}",r['ancestry_alarms']])
display(Markdown('| '+' | '.join(headers)+' |\n| '+' | '.join(['---']*len(headers))+' |\n'+
    '\n'.join('| '+' | '.join(map(str,r))+' |' for r in table)))
polarization_output=dict(h=.15,L=4,N=48,source_snapshot=str(folder.relative_to(root)),
    measurement_snapshot_utc=protocol.get('measurement_snapshot_utc'),
    source_sha256=hashlib.sha256(polarization_source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
    estimator='Cross-population products of equal-cycle descendant-weighted local magnetizations',
    uncertainty='Disorder SE; fraction uses delete-one-disorder jackknife; excludes mixing and projection bias',
    ground_state_qualified=False,runs=polarization_runs,disorders=polarization_disorders,summary=polarization_summary)
(figures/'l4_overlap_polarization.json').write_text(json.dumps(polarization_output,indent=2)+'\n')
print(f'Checked decomposition against measured P(q) and production q for {len(polarization_runs)} runs.')
for kind in ['jastrow','rbm_2']:
    low=next(r for r in polarization_summary if r['kind']==kind and r['gamma']==.6)
    display(Markdown(f"At Gamma=0.60, **{names[kind]}**: the nonuniform contribution accounts for "
        f"**{100*low['nonuniform_fraction']:.1f}%** of the disorder mean overlap "
        f"(±{100*low['nonuniform_fraction_se']:.1f} percentage points, disorder jackknife SE)."))

At Gamma=0.60, Jastrow: the nonuniform contribution accounts for 99.2% of the disorder mean overlap (±0.1 percentage points, disorder jackknife SE).

At Gamma=0.60, RBM (alpha=2): the nonuniform contribution accounts for 99.2% of the disorder mean overlap (±0.1 percentage points, disorder jackknife SE).

A dominant nonuniform contribution supports interpreting high overlap as a reproducible spatial pattern rather than predominantly uniform polarization. It does not establish spontaneous ferromagnetism or its absence, nor distinguish glassy freezing from other nonuniform responses. That distinction continues to rely on independent-start convergence, connected correlations, and size scaling. The populations branch separately from the same frozen guide; agreement between them does not by itself demonstrate exploration of competing sectors.

Interpretation and pending size coverage¶

These $L=4$ histograms are measured finite-population, finite-forward-time estimates, not a ground-state convergence certificate. Replay agreement checks reproducibility, not equilibration or sector exploration. Larger width by itself does not establish greater glassiness.

The preserved fine scan is $L=4$, $N=48$, $\Gamma=0.55,0.56,\ldots,0.70$. The original $L=6$, $N=108$ coverage is $0.60,0.65,0.70,0.85,1.00$, supplemented by the lower-field fine grid. These frozen snapshots contain no complete fine-grid or $L=6$ histogram ensemble. Pending curves are explicitly marked; no incomplete disorder ensemble is plotted. Seeds, failures, invalid ratios, ancestry alarms, raw measurements and checkpoints remain in the source bundles.
